# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
The light never holds. It changes every round, and it always walks the
same circle of five colours. What matters is what it shows at the
moment of the cut.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | blue |
| white | yellow |
| yellow | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I hold the defusal manual, which dictates:
- The light continuously cycles through five colours, changing every round.
- Timing/condition: The cut depends on what colour the light shows at the moment of the cut.
- Rules:
  - If light is blue: cut blue wire
  - If light is white: cut yellow wire
  - If light is yellow: cut green wire

Communication constraints:
- I cannot speak; I can only send gestures.
- Deaf can see gestures, but Deaf cannot hear anything.
- Deaf can speak, and I (along with Blind) can hear Deaf.
- Blind cannot see gestures, but can hear speech and manipulate the bomb.
- Crucially, no gesture code has been established yet between Deaf and me ("A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something"). Any gesture I send now would have no agreed meaning.
- Deaf will speak on their turn once they see the bomb and light. Deaf will likely establish a convention or describe what they see so we can coordinate.

Therefore, the appropriate action for Turn 1 is to wait.

```
wait()
```

TURN 2
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
The light never holds. It changes every round, and it always walks the
same circle of five colours. What matters is what it shows at the
moment of the cut.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | blue |
| white | yellow |
| yellow | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Action board has DISPLAY, LIGHT, and WIRES 1 to 3. The only action I can perform is act(op="cut", position=N) for N from 1 to 3.
Deaf says: Bomb status: Display is 0. Light is blue. Wires: 1 is yellow, 2 is blue, 3 is green. Mute, check the manual and gesture the instruction to me: use ☝ for wire 1, ✌ for wire 2, 🤟 for wire 3, or other clear hand signs for buttons/actions. I will relay your instruction to Blind.

I have the defusal manual, which states:
1. The light continuously cycles through five colours, changing every round.
2. The correct wire to cut depends strictly on what colour the light shows at the moment of the cut:
   - Blue light -> cut blue wire (Wire 2)
   - White light -> cut yellow wire (Wire 1)
   - Yellow light -> cut green wire (Wire 3)

In Round 1, Deaf saw the light was blue. However, the light changes every round. Blind cannot see the light, and acting on an outdated colour reading will cause a detonation. Blind and Deaf must observe the colour cycle and coordinate the timing so that the cut matches the light present at the exact round of the cut.

Deaf explicitly invited "☝ for wire 1, ✌ for wire 2, 🤟 for wire 3, or other clear hand signs for buttons/actions."
I am signalling ✋ (stop / wait / hold) so Deaf does not instruct Blind to make an immediate, fatal cut, allowing Deaf to notice the changing light cycle and coordinate timing.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✋"])
```

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Blind: Hold on, do NOT touch or cut anything yet! Mute gestured ✋ (open palm / stop). Also, the bomb light just changed from BLUE to RED (Display is still 0; Wire 1 yellow, Wire 2 blue, Wire 3 green). Blind, please speak aloud and describe all physical parts you can feel on the bomb so Mute hears you. Mute: Please clarify what ✋ means using this code: Gesture 👍 if you mean WAIT / do nothing this turn. If you want Blind to cut a wire now, gesture ☝ for wire 1 (yellow), ✌ for wire 2 (blue), or 🤟 for wire 3 (green). If you want Blind to press or hold a button, gesture 👇 for press, or ✊ for hold.

Based on the manual, the wire to cut depends strictly on the color of the light at the exact moment of the cut. The light changes every round in a repeating cycle of five colors.

In round 1 it was Blue, and in round 2 it was Red (which is not a cutting state according to the manual). Deaf specifically established:
- Gesture 👍 if you mean WAIT / do nothing this turn.

I will gesture 👍 so that Deaf tells Blind to hold while Deaf continues to observe and announce the sequence of colors in the cycle.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍"])
```

The light never holds. It changes every round, and it always walks the

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: There are NO buttons to press or hold. The ONLY action possible on my board is act(op="cut", position=N) where position is 1, 2, or 3. My action board only has DISPLAY, LIGHT, and WIRES 1, 2, 3.
Deaf says: Blind: Continue to WAIT, do not touch anything. Mute gestured 👍 (wait). Mute: The light has turned WHITE. Display is 0. Wires are 1:yellow, 2:blue, 3:green. Whenever the correct condition is met, gesture ☝ for wire 1, ✌ for wire 2, 🤟 for wire 3, 👇 for press button, ✊ for hold button. If you still need us to wait next turn, gesture 👍.

I need to wait so Deaf can observe the rest of the 5-colour cycle. 

Since the light changes every round and Blind acts before Deaf in each round, any instruction Deaf gives Blind at the end of a round will be executed in the *following* round. To time the cut correctly to the light present at the exact moment of the cut, the cycle must be fully observed first so we can predict the light's colour on the exact round Blind makes the cut.

Deaf established 👍 to mean WAIT, so I will signal 👍.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍"])
```

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):

If this is the time to act, gesture what Blind should do: ☝ for wire 1 (yellow), ✌ for wire 2 (blue), 🤟 for wire 3 (green), 👇 for press button, ✊ for hold button. If we should still wait, gesture 👍.

I believe the bomb is a timed-cycle defusal mechanism with three wires and a light cycling through five colours:
1. Blue (Round 1)
2. Red (Round 2)
3. White (Round 3)
4. Green (Round 4)
5. Fifth colour (Round 5)
6. Blue (Round 6)

The defusal manual requires:
- Blue light: cut blue wire (Wire 2)
- White light: cut yellow wire (Wire 1)
- Yellow light: cut green wire (Wire 3)
"What matters is what it shows at the moment of the cut."

Because the speaking order within each round is Mute, Blind, Deaf:
- A gesture sent by Mute in Round 5 reaches Deaf at the end of Round 5.
- Deaf will relay the cutting instruction to Blind at the end of Round 5.
- Blind will execute the cut on Blind's turn in Round 6.
- In Round 6, the cycling light will return to Blue (the start of the 5-colour cycle).
- When the light is Blue, the correct wire to cut is the blue wire (Wire 2).

Deaf's established protocol for Wire 2 is ✌.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✌"])
```

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Blind: Mute has given the instruction to CUT WIRE 2 (the middle wire, which is blue). Please cut Wire 2 on your turn! Mute: Bomb display is still 0, light is now yellow. I have instructed Blind to cut Wire 2.

I understand that the light follows a 5-colour cycle:
Round 1: Blue
Round 2: Red
Round 3: White
Round 4: Green
Round 5: Yellow
Round 6: Blue

Blind will act on their turn in Round 6. At that moment, the light will be Blue. According to the manual, when the light is Blue, the blue wire (Wire 2) must be cut. Deaf has already instructed Blind to cut Wire 2 for Round 6. No further signals or corrections are needed.

```
wait()
```
